suffix: Night. Hyper-realistic 16:9 film photograph, fine grain, no lens flares. No people, no text, no lettering, no logos.
rows: Low at robot height on the edge of a wrecked English town at night after a battle: crashed grey drones smoking on wet tarmac in the foreground, and through the smoke a long column of red-hooded robots marching out of the town towards camera in rain. The only light is the red glow of the fires in the wreckage.

High aerial over an English town's ring road at night: the town is dark, every street light out, and long rivers of red-robed hooded robots flow out of it along every road like spokes, small fires still burning in the town centre as the one warm light.

Over the slate roofs and chimneys of a dark terraced English town at night, smoke drifting across the foreground; far beyond on a mountain the great ring-shaped eye is lit, its white aperture and red rim lights the brightest thing in frame, and red robes fill the streets between the houses below.

A red-hooded robot in the near foreground at frame left, rain on its robe and metal face, red eyes lit; behind it a crashed drone burns on a motorway hard shoulder and the column of robed robots passes in the dark. The fire is the only light.

An empty crossroads in an English town at night, a single traffic light still changing on its pole, and beneath it red-hooded robots marching past in close ranks through the puddles. The traffic light is the one named light; every window behind is dark.

From a motorway footbridge at night looking down a British motorway: all six lanes filled to the horizon with marching red-robed robots, their red eyes running away into the distance like tail lights, no vehicles anywhere, the gantries dark.

Aerial over a deep green Welsh valley at night: the valley floor is a winding river of red-robed robots between dark hills, a dark village of terraced houses along the slope, a single searchlight from a hovering ship the only light.

Inside an empty British football stadium at night, the floodlights on: the pitch and every stand filled with red-hooded robots standing in silent rows where the crowd used to be. Wide from the top of the stand.

A long red-brick terraced street in a northern English town at night, every front door and window dark, red-hooded robots standing in ranks filling the street from wall to wall to the far end. One street lamp is the light.

Very high aerial over the English countryside at night: the patchwork of fields between dark hedgerows, and every field filled solid with red-robed robots in a grid like a parade ground, the parade ground grown into the whole country, to the horizon, one searchlight beam crossing.
Above the clouds at night: hundreds of dark disc ships hovering in layers to the horizon, white searchlight beams pointing down through the cloud deck, a thin moon behind as the one cold light.
Looking straight down from among a fleet of ships at night: through gaps between the dark hulls, far below, the red army fills the English landscape, the ships' searchlights falling on it.

From a dark English high street at night looking up: the whole sky is a ceiling of ship undersides, hull after hull with rows of white lights, no stars visible, red-robed robots in ranks in the street below.

Wide at night: the great ring-shaped eye on its mountain with fleets of ships circling it like a storm system, a lightning flash inside the clouds, the eye's white aperture the bright centre of the frame.

White chalk cliffs on the English south coast at night, the sea black below, and fleets of ships coming in over the water in layers from the horizon, their searchlights sweeping the waves and the cliff face.

The same satellite from the reference image in orbit, but now above the night side of the Earth: Britain and Europe below in darkness, and every city light is deep red instead of gold, red lines tracing the roads between them. The planet is occupied.

The same satellite from the reference image small in the foreground above the night side of the Earth, a thin ring of red light running along the whole curve of the planet's horizon like the rim of the great eye, red lights scattered across the land below.

Looking down past the solar wing of the same satellite from the reference image onto the British Isles at night from orbit: the islands outlined and filled with red points of light, the sea black, the satellite's panels lit faintly red from below.
From orbit beside the same satellite from the reference image: dark disc ships rising out of the atmosphere past it, and behind them the night side of the Earth glowing red across every continent.

The whole night side of the Earth seen from far out in space, every continent covered in red light where the city lights should be, and the same satellite from the reference image a small dark silhouette against it.
